text: Jupiter is moving through your 1st house, which happens for about a year out of every twelve. This is the part of your chart that is simply you: your body, your bearing, the face you show a room, the things you dare to begin. While Jupiter is here, the volume on all of that turns up. You feel more confident than you did last year, more willing to speak first, ask for more, and start what you had been circling. Other people notice. Something in you reads as warmer and luckier than usual, and strangers tend to give you openings you did not have to argue for. Astrologers have long treated this pass as the start of a new twelve-year chapter, and it tends to feel that way: old versions of yourself come loose at the seams, and a bigger one wants room. The classic use of this year is to launch. Put your name on things. Take the meeting, make the introduction, let yourself be seen wanting what you want. Enthusiasm is genuinely contagious now, and efforts that depend on other people believing in you go better than they usually do. The classic misuse is excess. Jupiter enlarges whatever it touches, and in the 1st house that includes appetite, promises, and self-regard. You can gain weight in a year like this, overbook yourself, and talk past the point where listening would have served. Confidence can round up into carelessness, because when everything seems to be working you stop checking whether it actually is. None of that cancels the gift; it just names the tax. Somewhere in the middle of the pass, Jupiter often slows and backs up for a stretch. Those months feel quieter, and they are for digesting: which of the new starts deserve your next decade, and which were just the mood talking. When the planet moves on, the door does not slam. What you began while it was here keeps growing on its own, and the rest of the twelve-year round tends to develop the seeds this season planted. So plant deliberately. Choose the two or three enlargements you would still want in five years, feed those, and let the rest stay pleasant weather. A year from now you will be carrying whatever you said yes to. Make sure it is something you are glad to carry.

For roughly a year, Jupiter is passing through your 2nd house, the part of your chart that handles money, possessions, and your private sense of what you are worth. Tradition ranks this among the better stretches for income in the twelve-year round. Earnings tend to grow, or chances to grow them appear: a raise becomes possible, a side income opens, clients arrive, or something you own gains value. Just as often the shift is inner. You start believing you deserve more, and that belief changes how you charge, what you ask for, and which offers you stop settling for. Generosity swells too. You pick up more checks, give better gifts, and enjoy your money in a way leaner years did not allow. The warning built into this transit is as old as the good news: whatever comes in, spending rises to meet it and then some. Jupiter makes the future feel funded, so the purchase feels safe, the loan feels light, and the balance feels like next month's problem. People often end a 2nd house Jupiter year having earned noticeably more and kept none of it. Knowing that in advance is most of the protection. The deeper work of the pass is about worth rather than cash. Notice what you are actually valuing with your money now, because the spending pattern is a confession: comfort, status, freedom, other people's approval. Jupiter here invites you to fund what you would still respect in ten years, and to let your sense of being enough rest on something steadier than the number in the account. If the planet retraces its steps partway through, a money question from earlier in the year comes back for a second decision, and the review usually improves the terms. Asking, negotiating, and building the skill that raises your rate all suit the season, since the people who set prices on your work are better disposed than usual. By the time Jupiter leaves, the opportunities thin back to normal. What stays is whatever you turned the flow into: a cushion, a tool, a debt, or a very good year of dinners. All four are possible. The transit only supplies the abundance. What it becomes is your call, and the choosing is where you grow.

Your daily rounds get busier and more interesting while Jupiter moves through your 3rd house, a pass that runs about a year. This is the chart's district of words, errands, siblings, neighbors, short trips, and the everyday mind, and Jupiter arriving here is like a good teacher walking into a restless classroom. Curiosity comes back. You read more, ask more, sign up for the course, finally learn the software or the language. Ideas that used to feel like homework start to feel like appetite. It is one of the friendlier times in the twelve-year cycle for anything built from language: writing, teaching, selling, presenting, or simply making your case. Your words carry further than usual, and people seem readier to hear you out. The traffic runs both ways. Calls, messages, invitations, and paperwork multiply, and the calendar fills with small commitments that are each easy and collectively crushing. Jupiter's vice here is scatter: ten open tabs, four half-finished projects, opinions issued faster than they are checked. You can also promise more in conversation than you remember agreeing to, which is how a lucky year quietly becomes an overdue one. Connections close to home often warm up under this transit. A sibling relationship can ease or deepen, a neighbor becomes a friend, the local scene turns out to hold more than you thought. Short trips repay themselves, because the change of scene feeds the mind. If Jupiter backtracks partway through the year, a piece of writing or a stalled conversation gets a second draft, and second drafts under this sky are usually the better ones. The growth on offer is a bigger mind, not just a busier one. The difference is made by what you do with what you take in: the note kept, the idea followed for a month instead of an afternoon, the opinion revised out loud. Let the curiosity land somewhere. A year of this weather can leave you with a credential, a manuscript, a repaired family thread, or a phone full of tabs. The hours are the same either way, and while Jupiter is here you get more said, more learned, and more connected per hour than you usually do.

For about a year, Jupiter settles into your 4th house, the base of the chart: home, family, roots, and the private self your public one stands on. Growth turns inward and downward during this pass. The classic outer events are real and common: a move to a bigger or better place, a renovation, a household that expands, a family matter that finally goes well, property dealings that favor you. Home becomes a place where good things happen rather than just where you recover from them. Hospitality tends to increase, and your table gets longer. The inner shift matters at least as much. Jupiter here fattens the root system. Old family stories can reopen in a kinder light, an estrangement can soften, and you may find yourself more generous with your own history, better able to see what the people who raised you were working with. A feeling of basic safety often grows this year, the settled kind that later ambitions quietly stand on. Tradition calls the 4th the end of the matter, and under Jupiter endings here tend to be graceful ones: a chapter closes more kindly than you expected. The excess to watch is weight at the base. Houses can swallow money under this transit, and the bigger place, the extra room, and the renovation that grows in scope all feel more affordable than they are. Family generosity can slide into rescuing, where you become the household's sponsor and quietly resent it. Comfort itself can overgrow, making the couch so pleasant that the outer life thins. If the planet retraces its path mid-year, domestic plans get revised, and the revision usually rights the scale. Emotionally, this is one of the better years in the cycle for foundation work: honest conversations with parents or children, grief given its room, making a home actually yours rather than a storage unit with a bed in it. You grow through this pass by letting the enlargement reach the root and not just the square footage. When Jupiter moves on, the visible changes stay visible, but the quieter gain is the one you will use longest: more room inside, a past that takes up less of the house, and ground under you that holds.

Jupiter spends about a year in your 5th house, and the theme of that year is delight: romance, play, creative work, children, and everything you do because you want to rather than because you must. Warmth returns to parts of life that may have gone dutiful. If you are open to love, this is one of the friendlier stretches in the twelve-year round for meeting someone, and attractions that begin now tend to be generous and fun before they are anything else. Existing relationships often remember how to play. Creative work swells under this sky. Projects want to be bigger, audiences respond better, and the confidence to show your work, a different muscle from making it, comes easier than usual. Children tend to bring more than they cost this year, whether your own kids flourish, a new child enters the picture for some, or younger people simply seek you out and repay attention with liveliness. Your own inner kid gets louder too, and that is mostly the point. The famous risk of the transit is too much of a good thing. Jupiter in the 5th can gamble, at actual tables but also in the wider sense: the flirtation that outgrows its container, the speculative bet sized by mood, the pleasure calendar that eats the working one. Fun is the teacher here, not an exemption from consequences, and enjoyment chased frantically stops being enjoyment. The year works better approached as abundance than as scarcity you must grab. If Jupiter loops backward for part of the pass, a romance or a creative project from earlier in the year returns for reconsideration, often in improved form. What this transit is quietly for is enlarging your capacity for joy, which in adults shrinks by neglect rather than by age. Somewhere in this year is the thing you loved doing before anyone graded you on anything. Doing it again, at whatever level, is not a detour from your real life. It refills the tank your real life runs on. When the planet moves along, the parties thin out, but people who use the year well keep the habit it taught: making something, loving someone, and playing at full size, on purpose, without waiting for permission.

While Jupiter crosses your 6th house, roughly a year of its twelve-year round, the growth shows up in unglamorous places: your work, your workload, your habits, your health, and the daily machinery that keeps everything else running. Work usually improves first. More comes to you: responsibility, better projects, appreciative colleagues, sometimes a better position outright before any title catches up. Service is honored under this sky, and the reputation you build now, as the person who does the thing well and helps freely, compounds quietly for years. The volume is the hazard. Jupiter enlarges whatever house it occupies, and in the 6th that means the to-do list. Saying yes feels good and keeps feeling good right up until the calendar files a complaint. Overwork under a cheerful sky is still overwork, and the body keeps the ledger even when the mood does not. Which points to the other classic theme: health. On the whole this transit favors it. Vitality tends to run higher, recovery comes easier, and the routines you have been postponing take root more readily now, movement you actually like, food that treats you as someone with a future, sleep defended like an appointment. Jupiter's overdoing can also reach the plate and the sofa, so the same year that offers better habits will happily fund worse ones. The difference lies only in what you feed. Daily life itself can grow sweeter in small ways: a better workspace, a pet, coworkers who become real company, the discovery that a tuned-up ordinary day is worth more than an occasional spectacular one. If the planet backs up mid-pass, routines you set earlier get tested and revised, and the second version usually fits better. The invitation of this transit is to find meaning in maintenance. Not to romanticize the grind, but to notice that competence is a form of generosity and that a life is mostly made of Tuesdays. People who use a 6th house Jupiter year well come out of it with work that fits better, a body that runs better, and days that hold more than they used to. The improvements are rarely dramatic on any given morning. Stacked for a year, they change the ground you stand on.

Partnership carries the growth while Jupiter travels through your 7th house, a pass of about a year that arrives once in twelve. This is the chart's meeting place: marriage and committed love, business partners, close collaborators, and the one-to-one bonds where another person can actually change your course. Under Jupiter, those bonds expand or arrive. If you are single and would rather not be, this is the traditional year for it, and the people drawn in now tend to bring benefit with them: openness, resources, perspective, doors. Established couples often take a growth step, a commitment, a shared venture, a renewed friendliness after a flat stretch. Working alliances flourish too, and the collaborator, agent, or advisor who shows up in a year like this is worth taking seriously. Others are simply better disposed toward you across a table, which makes the season favorable for agreements, negotiations, and settling disputes on decent terms. Even conflict tends to resolve more generously than it would at another time. The excess wears two faces here. One is overcommitment: promising a person more than you have checked you can give, merging plans, homes, or businesses on enthusiasm that has not yet met logistics. The other is outsourcing: handing a partner the job of being your growth, your confidence, or your luck, which flatters them for a month and burdens them for years. Jupiter in the 7th teaches that relationships enlarge people. It does not say they replace what each person still builds alone. If the planet retraces mid-year, a relationship question from earlier in the pass comes back for a second, wiser round, and agreements revisited then usually end fairer. It is worth noticing who you become around these bigger others: more generous is growth, more dependent is drift. When Jupiter moves on, the meetings it arranged remain. A marriage begun, a partnership signed, a rivalry ended, a friendship upgraded: these are the durable exports of the year. The skill it leaves behind, if you practice it, is bigger-heartedness at close range, the ability to let someone matter, to ask for real things, and to be asked in return without flinching.

Jupiter's year in your 8th house takes the growth somewhere quieter and deeper. This is the chart's shared vault: joint money, debts, taxes, inheritance, other people's resources, intimacy, and the psychological basement most people visit only when forced. Jupiter here tends to make the deep places generous rather than frightening. The material side is often plainly helpful. Matters involving shared or outside money go better than usual. A loan is approved, a debt gets easier terms, a settlement or an inheritance improves your position, or backing arrives for something you could not fund alone. It is a good year for cleaning up entanglements, insurance, taxes, and the dull paperwork of merged lives, because the other side is more flexible than it will be later. The same mood can loosen your borrowing standards. Easy credit in a confident season is how this transit sometimes leaves people worse off, so a lender's warmth deserves the same scrutiny you would give another year's coldness. Intimacy is the other half. Trust comes easier now, and closeness that has been stuck at a polite depth can open: franker talks, better sex, secrets set down, a willingness to actually merge rather than politely share space. Old griefs and fears are easier to face under this sky. Many people do their best inner work of the whole cycle during this pass, in counseling or in honest company, because Jupiter makes the descent feel survivable and even rewarding. Losses handled this year tend to leave meaning behind instead of only absence. If the planet backs over the same ground mid-year, a financial arrangement or an emotional reckoning returns for completion, and the second pass usually finishes what the first could only start. The growth offered here is the kind that does not show in photographs: fewer secrets running the machinery, cleaner agreements about what is mine, yours, and ours, and the discovery that depth rewards visitors. When Jupiter leaves, the surface life resumes its claim on your attention. What you keep is capacity: for honesty at close range, for endings that do not wreck you, and for holding shared things, money or hearts, with a steadier hand.

The horizon moves outward while Jupiter crosses your 9th house. This is the planet's favorite territory, the house of travel, higher learning, publishing, teaching, law, belief, and every question bigger than the week, and the pass lasts about a year in each twelve. Restlessness of the best kind sets in. The town feels small, the routine feels finished, and something in you wants distance: a real trip, a course of study, a body of ideas, a tradition worth arguing with. Under this sky, going usually works. Journeys taken now tend to pay for themselves in perspective, formal education favors you more than most years, and it is a friendlier season than usual for admissions, examinations, certifications, publishing, and legal matters, the arenas where judgment is passed on your case. Your own worldview is the real construction site. Beliefs you inherited get inspected, some are kept with better reasons, some are outgrown, and what fills the space feels chosen rather than issued. Teachers matter this year, and so does the moment you notice you have become one, since Jupiter in the 9th often puts you on both sides of the lectern. The overflow to watch is conviction. Fresh certainty is loud, and this transit can turn a learner into a preacher within a season: opinions issued from one book read, plans inflated from one good trip, the faith that being right excuses being unbearable. The cure is built into the house, because more learning humbles what one lesson inflated. Overreach is possible too, the grand plan announced before the ground is checked. If Jupiter retraces its route partway through, a study, a case, a publication, or a belief comes back for revision, and the revised version is usually the sounder one. What this year builds, used well, is a larger frame: a sense of what your life is about that can hold more contradiction than the old one could. That frame is the export. Trips end, courses finish, verdicts come in, but the way you answer the question of what it all means, refreshed now, steers the decade of choices that follows. Go far enough this year, in miles or in pages, that home looks different when you turn around.

Career weather turns favorable while Jupiter moves across your 10th house, the summit of the chart, where reputation, ambition, and public standing live. The pass runs about a year and comes once in twelve, and tradition ranks it among the best professional stretches in the whole cycle. What it tends to bring is visibility with a tailwind. Your work gets seen by people who can do something about it. Promotions, offers, launches, awards, new titles, and public moments cluster in years like this, and even where nothing dramatic lands, your standing quietly rises: your name comes up in rooms you are not in, attached to good sentences. Authority figures are better disposed toward you than usual, and it is a strong season for aiming higher than feels quite polite, since asks that would normally stall have a way of going through. The structural gift underneath the luck is clarity of aim. Jupiter here enlarges ambition itself, and many people finally admit the size of what they want during this transit. Admitting it is useful, because the year rewards a target. The risks are the summit's usual ones, enlarged. Overpromising to important people, taking the bigger role before checking what it costs at home, and believing your own coverage are the classic stumbles. Visibility cuts both ways, so a shortcut taken now is taken in public. Arrogance is the tax collector of this house, and it arrives precisely when things are going well. There is also the subtler trap of climbing a ladder faster only to confirm it leans on the wrong wall. If Jupiter reverses through this territory mid-year, a professional plan gets rethought, and the rethink usually aims the effort better. The lasting question of the pass is what you want to be responsible for in public, because Jupiter grows whatever you are doing at the top, suited to you or not. Success at the wrong thing is this transit's strangest gift, and noticing that counts as a win too. Handled honestly, the year leaves you with more than a better job. It leaves a reputation with weight, ambition you no longer apologize for, and a clearer answer when someone asks what you are building up there.

Your circle widens while Jupiter spends its year in your 11th house, the part of the chart that holds friendships, groups, communities, allies, and the hopes you are steering your life toward. The change is often simple to see: more people. Invitations increase, old friends resurface, new ones arrive through work, causes, teams, or scenes you finally join, and some of the people who show up in a year like this become fixtures for decades. The quality shifts too. Jupiter here draws helpful company, friends who open doors, tell you the useful truth, and think more of your prospects than you do. Whatever you are trying to build, this is the season when building it with others multiplies it: the group project, the association, the collective that gets further in a year than you got alone in three. Communities reward your investment now, and being generous inside a network, with introductions, credit, and effort, comes back with interest. The house also governs your hopes, and under Jupiter they enlarge. Goals that were sized for safety start to feel small, and the year invites a rewrite: what are you actually aiming your life at, and who would you have to know, and be, to get there. Old dreams sometimes return in feasible form. The excess to watch is social sprawl. You can spend the whole pass in rooms full of people and end it without one deepened friendship, popular and unaccompanied. Groups can also swallow judgment, since belonging feels so good under this sky that you may adopt a crowd's opinions or plans wholesale to keep the warmth. Choose your rooms with care, because you grow toward whatever your company assumes is normal. If Jupiter tracks backward for part of the year, a friendship or a group commitment from earlier in the pass gets reweighed, and what survives the reweighing is the keeping kind. When the planet moves on, the crowd thins to its true size. What remains, used well, is a better set of allies, a cause or community with your fingerprints on it, and hopes upgraded from what seemed available to what turns out, with help, to be possible.

Jupiter's pass through your 12th house is the quietest year of its twelve-year round, and one of the kindest, though it rarely looks that way from outside. This is the chart's back room: solitude, sleep, dreams, retreats, secrets, old sorrows, and everything that goes on in you before it goes on in the world. Growth continues through this year, but underground. Outwardly, life may go oddly still. Ambition loosens its grip, the social appetite thins, and you want more time alone than the people around you expect. That pull is the transit working. Jupiter here rewards retreat: rest, reflection, prayer or meditation if those are yours, long walks, honest counsel, any practice that lets the inner life speak first. The inner world becomes generous in return. Dreams get louder, forgiveness comes easier, and compassion widens, for others and eventually for yourself, which is usually the harder half. Old guilt and old grief soften enough to be handled and set down. Tradition also calls this the angel on the shoulder transit: help arrives unseen, troubles dissolve before they reach you, and kindnesses you did long ago come home in disguise. You may never trace the protection, but people often feel it. Endings belong to this house, and under Jupiter they tend to be merciful. It is a fitting year to finish things, a role, a residence, a resentment, a chapter, because the planet's next move carries it into your 1st house and opens a new round, and the new round opens better if your hands are empty. The risks are escapist. The same softness that heals can blur, and drifting, oversleeping, secret comforts, and quiet avoidance can absorb the whole pass if nothing in you keeps a rudder. Compassion without boundaries also invites a certain kind of taker. If Jupiter backtracks partway through, something you thought was finished asks for one more round of letting go; give it the round. Measured by the outer scoreboard, this year may show little. Measured rightly, it can return the most valuable thing in the cycle: a self with its debts of feeling settled, rested and forgiven, ready for the beginning already on its way.
